The password security practice described in the text is highly insecure. Using the same password for every account is a major vulnerability because if one account is compromised, all other accounts using that same password are immediately at risk. This practice is known as password reuse. While changing the password monthly might seem like a good habit, it does not mitigate the risk of credential stuffing or data breaches from other services. A strong password policy requires unique, complex passwords for each account, ideally managed with a password manager.

A group of crows is called a murder.
